rule.description: "6:163: There is no obligation to repair the damage on the ground of a tortious act if the violated standard of behaviour does not intend to offer protection against damage as suffered by the injured person." In other words: this law aims to keep the usage of the tortious act within reasonable bounds. The basis on which a claim is made (the law that is called by the victim), has to be the same basis as the called reason (The reason the victim thinks he is violated).
The standard of behaviour, that has been violated, needs to intend to offer protection against the claimed damage.

question.description: Does the broken norm, being the law or social conduct whose imposed duty is violated, aim to protect the victim?
Does the broken norm, being the law or social conduct whose imposed duty is violated, aim to protect against the type of damage. i.e. financial or physical?
Does the broken norm, being the law or social conduct whose imposed duty is violated, aim to prevent the manner at which the victim claims to be damaged.
